vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: Borrowed from Aramaic, in Classical Syriac ܫܘܫ (šawweš), and also with that consonantism in Jewish Palestinian Aramaic, Classical Mandaic, for older Aramaic שׁבשׁ (šbš) in Jewish Babylonian Aramaic, Jewish Literary Aramaic, Christian Palestinian Aramaic, Classical Mandaic, Biblical Aramaic.
Derived from the passive participle of شَوَّشَ (šawwaša, “to muddle”).

Etymology tree
Arabic شَاش (šāš)
Proto-Afroasiatic
Proto-Semitic
Arabic ـِيّ (-iyy)
Proto-Afroasiatic *-t
Proto-Semitic *-at-
Arabic ـَة (-a)
Arabic ـِيَّة (-iyya)
Arabic شاشية
From شَاش (šāš, “muslin”) + ـِيَّة (-iyya), the cap originally made of muslin.
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.
